clue.text: Ungrammatical claim of GP that's regularly drunk?

parts.note: saying 'me' where grammar wants 'I' is the ungrammatical way to claim an identity
a GP (general practitioner) is a doctor, informally a doc

explanation.surface: A family doctor boasts, badly phrased, about something he drinks routinely.
explanation.walkthrough: The ungrammatical claim is 'Me doc!' rather than 'I am a doctor'. 'That's regularly drunk' looks like a jibe at the GP but defines a claret.
explanation.definitionFit: Médoc is a widely consumed Bordeaux red wine, so it is a drink taken regularly.

clue.text: Funny, gold ring being found in mull

indicators.note: things found in something else sit within it, so these pieces go inside the outer word

parts.note: mull is a type of humus, loose forest-floor soil
OR is gold in heraldry
a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone finds an amusing gold ring while mulling something over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mull' looks like a verb or the Scottish island, but it is the soil scientist's word for a kind of humus.
explanation.definitionFit: Something humorous is comic and amusing, a straightforward synonym for funny.

clue.text: Poor London lass is second to enter this Pacific country

indicators.note: one piece enters another by going inside it
poor here means badly made or in bad shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: An impoverished girl from London is the next to arrive in a Pacific nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' makes the anagram SOLONISLANDS; 'second' is the informal mo, as in 'wait a mo', not the ordinal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Solomon Islands are a sovereign island nation in the south-west Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Armed vessel at end of line in quiet watercourse

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

indicators.note: one piece sits in another, so these letters go inside the watercourse word

parts.note: a river is a natural watercourse

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A gunboat waits at the end of the line on a peaceful stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A privateer was a privately owned ship armed and licensed by a government to attack enemy shipping.

clue.text: Son leaves county, having initially received letter?

indicators.note: when one letter leaves a word it is taken out of it

parts.note: a shire is an English county

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A son moves away from the county after first getting a letter in the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' is a mail item on the surface but means one who lets, as a landlord lets property.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rents something out lets it, so one who hires out is a letter in the crossword sense.

clue.text: Change the least amount of cash for vegetable

parts.note: to change is to turn, as milk turns
the smallest sum is one penny, 1p, with the numeral one written as the letter I

explanation.surface: Swap the tiniest bit of money for something from the greengrocer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' suggests coins in the surface; here it is the verb meaning to become different.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnip is a root vegetable with white flesh.

clue.text: RAF officer filling in month in charge of a plant

indicators.note: something filling in a space goes inside it

parts.note: Jan is short for January
PO is a Pilot Officer in the Royal Air Force

explanation.surface: An air force officer takes over during a month, responsible for a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: Japonica is the common name for the flowering quince shrub and some other Japanese plants.

clue.text: Insist chief can, when touring area

parts.note: main means chief or principal

indicators.note: a word touring something goes all round it, so it encloses the other piece

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: The boss insists he can manage while travelling round the region.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a point is to assert or insist on it firmly.

clue.text: Individual beginning to snooze by fireplace

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: an ingle is a fireside or hearth, as in inglenook

explanation.surface: Someone starts to doze off beside the hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: Single and individual both mean one on its own.

clue.text: Further thought blocking return of main recesses

indicators.note: a piece blocking another sits in its path, inside it
return makes the word read back the other way

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open sea
PS, a postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter

explanation.surface: An afterthought stops the main plan coming back to some alcoves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return of' gives AES; 'main' is the poetic word for the sea, not 'principal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Apses are semicircular recesses, typically at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Fuss relating to porridge

parts.note: a stir is a commotion or fuss
about means concerning, relating to

explanation.surface: A commotion about breakfast oats.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirabout is an Irish name for oatmeal porridge stirred while cooking.

clue.text: Where getting on's trendy, enthralling Head of Harrow?

definitions.text: Where getting on's trendy, enthralling Head of Harrow?

parts.note: getting on a bus or train is boarding, and the 's adds an S

indicators.note: enthralling literally holds captive, so the word encloses the other piece

parts.note: cool means fashionable, trendy

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A school where getting ahead is fashionable, captivating even Harrow's headmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a famous English boarding school, so the whole clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A school where pupils live in term time is a residential school, and Harrow is a classic example.

clue.text: Runner showing increased complacency skirting lake

indicators.note: skirting goes round the edge of, so the outer word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: smugger means more smug, more complacent
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: An athlete becomes more and more self-satisfied while running round a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' looks like an athlete, but a runner also smuggles goods, as in gun-runner.
explanation.definitionFit: A smuggler runs contraband across borders, so he is a runner in that sense.

clue.text: Note by accredited agency ultimately providing run-down?

parts.note: to note something is to see it

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of each word

explanation.surface: A memo from a certified agency ends up giving a summary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run-down' suggests a summary report, but here means shabby.
explanation.definitionFit: A seedy place is shabby and dilapidated, in a run-down condition.

clue.text: Old Asian's son, a poet and imam, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters given are only one possible arrangement, so they are mixed up

explanation.surface: An ancient Asian's offspring is both a poet and a Muslim leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'; 'and' joins the fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mesopotamian was an inhabitant of ancient Mesopotamia, the land between the Tigris and Euphrates in Asia.

clue.text: Capital husband invested in food shop

indicators.note: money invested in something is put into it, so this letter goes inside

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a shop for prepared foods

explanation.surface: A married man puts his money into a delicatessen in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi, via New Delhi, is the capital of India.

clue.text: Orchestra member Verlaine, for example, talked of

indicators.note: talked of means spoken, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: Paul Verlaine was a French poet of the Symbolist movement

explanation.surface: A member of an orchestra discusses the French poet Verlaine.
explanation.definitionFit: A percussionist who plays the cymbals is a player in an orchestra.

clue.text: Sound name for a noted scorer

indicators.note: a sound version of a word is one that matches it when spoken

parts.note: a handle is slang for a name

explanation.surface: A famous goalscorer has a name that sounds right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scorer' suggests sport; a composer scores music, and 'noted' hints at musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: George Frideric Handel was a celebrated composer, someone who writes scores of music.

clue.text: Northerly wind restricting one's faulty hearing

indicators.note: restricting confines, so the outer word holds the other piece inside

parts.note: the mistral is a cold north wind of southern France
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cold wind from the north limits someone's ability to hear properly.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is'. 'Hearing' looks like listening but is a court hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistrial is a trial invalidated by an error, so a court hearing that is faulty.

clue.text: Gigantic bird swallowing a hard fish

indicators.note: something swallowing another takes it inside

parts.note: the roc is an enormous mythical bird from Arabian legend
H stands for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A giant bird gulps down a tough fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The roach is a freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Lackey finally collapsing after endless stress?

indicators.note: without its end means the last letter is removed

parts.note: to underline something is to stress it

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A servant finally breaks down after constant pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: An underling is a subordinate, a lackey who serves others.

clue.text: Verbally, quote books accommodated in decorative manner

indicators.note: accommodated means housed, so these pieces sit inside the outer word

parts.note: orally means spoken, verbally
to quote as an example is to name it
NT is the New Testament, books of the Bible

explanation.surface: In speech, cite books that are set out in an ornate way.
explanation.definitionFit: Done ornamentally means done as decoration, in an ornate fashion.

clue.text: Mental aberration, bishop leaving in wild weather

indicators.note: something leaving is taken away

parts.note: a brainstorm is a sudden mental disturbance or aberration
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop has a mental lapse and walks out into a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainstorm is a storm with heavy rain, a spell of wild weather.

clue.text: Representing Lagos, rich members of small government?

indicators.note: representing suggests the letters stand for something else in a new form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wealthy people speak for Lagos.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as playful: an oligarchy is government by a few.
explanation.definitionFit: Oligarchs belong to an oligarchy, rule by a small group, so they are its members.

clue.text: Island GP's extraordinary desire for kitchen scraps

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the ordinary, so the letters are taken out of their order

parts.note: the plural-looking GP's supplies GPS
will means desire or wish

explanation.surface: A doctor on an island has a strange wish for leftover food.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigswill is waste food from kitchens fed to pigs.

clue.text: One dancing with delight, perhaps, in this old golf club

definitions.meaning: someone who jigs, dancing a lively jig for joy
an iron with a narrow face, formerly used in golf

explanation.definitionFit: A jigger is one who jigs, and also a lofted iron in early golf.

clue.text: Sporting people initially given gear for shoot

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of each word

parts.note: rig means equipment or gear

explanation.surface: Sporty folk are first handed their kit for a shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' suggests hunting with guns, but here is a plant's young shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a small shoot or twig of a plant.

clue.text: Bleaching agent, an antipodean example?

parts.note: Oz is informal for Australia, in the antipodes
one can stand for an example, as in 'that's a good one'

explanation.surface: Is a bleaching agent found down under?
explanation.walkthrough: 'An antipodean example' reads as 'an Oz one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is a strong oxidiser used to bleach and disinfect.
